reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports room-temperature friction and wear reduction and tribocatalytic activity on a steel substrate, but provides no data on high-temperature performance, coating integrity at elevated temperatures, or application to HEA substrates. The key premise of wide-temperature-range effectiveness is entirely unsupported.
premises: A 2D TMD HEA coating can be deposited uniformly on HEA components via air-spray or similar process
The coating has a layered structure with weak interlayer bonding enabling easy basal plane sliding
The coating reduces COF and wear rate at room temperature under ambient conditions
Stress-induced tribocatalytic reactions continuously refresh a lubricious tribofilm during sliding
The coating remains effective and intact across a wide temperature range (ambient to 600–800 °C)
